findings.claim: 'a repository named `constructor` or `toString` — both legal GitHub names, both accepted by repoNameFromRemoteUrl — would otherwise read an inherited function out of it and throw at the first .filter' (same sentence in .changeset/signon-derive-seat-2801.md:10 and in the test comment at orchestration-resolver.test.ts:696)
findings.counterexample: The key is lower-cased at orchestration-resolver.ts:216 BEFORE the lookup, so `toString` becomes `tostring`, which is not an Object.prototype member. Simulating the pre-fold line verbatim: constructor -> key `constructor` -> THREW TypeError: mapped.filter is not a function; toString -> key `tostring` -> OK, mapped=[]; hasOwnProperty -> key `hasownproperty` -> OK, mapped=[]; __proto__ -> key `__proto__` -> THREW TypeError. So the `toString` half of the rationale is false in all three places, and 2 of the 4 names in the new test loop (orchestration-resolver.test.ts:698) pass on the PRE-fold code — non-falsifying rows. The control as a whole would still have failed pre-fold on iteration 1 (`constructor`), so it has teeth. Also imprecise: for `__proto__` the pre-fold read returns Object.prototype, an OBJECT, not a 'function'. Folded: the comment, the changeset and the test name the two lower-case prototype members that reach the map (`constructor`, `__proto__`) and say why camel-case members cannot.

findings.claim: the test named '--json emits ONE stdout object in both arms with the same exit codes, and nothing on stderr' proves nothing reaches stderr
findings.counterexample: `stderr` is fed ONLY by the `vi.spyOn(log,'error')` mock (lines 109-112). `expect(refused.stderr).toBe('')` therefore proves exactly 'log.error was not called' — the same proposition as `expect(refused.tags).toEqual([])` on the next line — and CANNOT observe console.error, process.stderr.write, or a child process's stderr. The harness DOES disclose the proxy (lines 87-92: 'log.error is the CLI's stderr channel'), and the property holds today (real CLI: 0 bytes on stderr in all three json arms, verified), so this is an assertion-strength gap, not a false claim: a future console.error added anywhere on the path (deriveSeatStatuses, a resolver warning print) would pass this test. Folded: the harness also spies process.stderr.write and console.error and the json test asserts both stayed silent.
